title: szeretném, ha + Conditional: Saying What You Wish Would Happen

sections.title: Building on Jobb lenne, ha...
sections.content: You already built hypothetical sentences with Jobb lenne, ha... (A2) — a wish about a situation, stated impersonally. szeretném, ha... does the same job, but names YOU as the one who wants it: szeretném steps into the place of jobb lenne, and the ha-clause still takes the conditional, exactly the way you already learned. Szeretném, ha sikerülne a tervem literally reads "I would like it, if my plan succeeded" — the natural Hungarian way to say "I wish my plan would succeed."

sections.title: szeretném, ha...
rows: I wish my plan would succeed.
I wish I had time for everything.
Szeretném, ha könnyebb lenne az élet.

items.english: I wish my dream would come true.

items.spanish: Szeretném, ha kevesebb akadály állna az utamban.
items.english: I wish there were fewer obstacles in my way.

sections.content: The verb inside the ha-clause agrees with its own subject, not with szeretném — sikerülne agrees with a tervem ("my plan", 3rd person), not with "I". Only szeretném itself stays fixed in the 1st person, since you're always the one doing the wishing.
